title: E-Tray Exercise 2
role: a new consultant joining the Entrepreneur Fast-Track team at Cannon Carlisle to replace Odette Lawson, working on the afternoon of Friday 24 January 2014

opts.t: No response required.
opts.why: Second most effective: the e-mail from Sally Hayes does not need any further input. Replying would be polite, but this option shows effective prioritising within the time limit.

opts.t: Thank you very much for welcoming me to the Company and for the additional information you thoughtfully included. I look forward to working with you in the near future.
opts.why: Most effective: it shows the candidate understood Sally’s message while staying polite and courteous.

opts.t: Thank you very much for welcoming me to the Company. The documents you mentioned sound extremely helpful and I am keen to have a look at them, where would I be able to locate them? I look forward to working with you in the near future.
opts.why: Not appropriate: Sally’s message says the documents were attached to the e-mail.

opts.t: Thank you for welcoming me to the company, I really appreciate your kind and thoughtful e-mail. Not to worry about the departmental and structural information, there is no rush to replace my predecessor’s name with my own. As for my willingness to take up the position so quickly, I am just enthusiastic to be working with such an established company and am eager to apply myself to the role. I look forward to working with you in the near future.
opts.why: Least effective: the e-mail does not need a lengthy reply, and writing one shows poor time allocation under a strict time limit.

opts.t: I appreciate that you have to re-arrange a lot following Odette Lawson’s departure, I will happily have whatever she ordered so as not to cause a fuss.
opts.why: Second most effective: it tries to make things easier for Amira, but Odette may not have given her menu choices before leaving, which would cause more correspondence.

opts.t: I would like to have Olive and Falafel Parcels, Marinated Chicken Kebabs and Baklava. Thank you.
opts.why: Most effective: all three items are on the menu for 7th February, the launch date.

opts.t: I would like to have Stuffed Vine Leaves, Feta and Aubergine Tart and Rizagolo. Thank you.
opts.why: Not appropriate: these items are not on the menu for 7th February.

opts.t: I am sorry but I am unable to attend the Launch Party. Please accept my apologies.
opts.why: Least effective: the Minutes (Document 2) say attendance is mandatory for Entrepreneur Fast-Track staff.

items.t: E-mail 3: Laura Clarke – IMPORTANT (tech support for Myro Ltd)

opts.t: I recommend SysCo.
opts.why: Least effective: the cost is vastly over budget, and Robert’s e-mail says Myro cannot move on price.

opts.t: I recommend Capitech Ltd.
opts.why: Not appropriate: Myro Ltd need 24/7 access to a helpdesk (Document 3).

opts.t: I recommend Alliance On-line.
opts.why: Most effective: it comes closest to all of Myro’s requirements while staying within the £205 monthly budget. A performance rate over 70% is only “preferable”, so 69% still meets the criteria.

opts.t: I recommend DigiCorp.
opts.why: Second most effective: it is only just outside the specified budget.

items.t: E-mail 4: Alan Walker – Entrepreneur Fast-Track Meetings

opts.t: I am afraid that I will be unable to attend.
opts.why: Least effective: no attempt to reschedule, and attendance is mandatory.

opts.t: I look forward to meeting with you on Friday at 11am.
opts.why: Most effective: it confirms the slot that was allocated to Odette Lawson, whom the candidate is replacing (Document 7).

opts.t: I look forward to meeting with you on Thursday at 4pm.
opts.why: Not appropriate: that time is allocated to another employee.

opts.t: I am afraid that I will be unable to attend at that time, although I would be available for a meeting on Thursday at 3pm if convenient.
opts.why: Second most effective: it tries to reschedule to an appropriate time.

opts.t: I would be inclined to agree with your e-mail, it does seem likely that the EFT team would be let go in the event of failure.
opts.why: Least effective: there is no evidence for the claim, and agreeing worries an employee who plans to raise it with the whole team and lower morale.

opts.t: I haven’t heard anything; I doubt that there is a reason to be concerned.
opts.why: Second most effective: it reassures a worried colleague, but you cannot say there is no reason for concern without evidence either way.

opts.t: No Response Required.
opts.why: Not appropriate: the e-mail is about a sensitive matter, and leaving it unanswered could lead Robert to share his worries and lower the team’s morale.

opts.t: I haven’t heard anything. Still, we should take this opportunity to do our best and ensure that the EFT programme is a success.
opts.why: Most effective: it reassures a worried colleague while motivating him and encouraging a positive outlook.

opts.t: In line with the new budget, I recommend SysCo.
opts.why: Least effective: still vastly over budget.

opts.t: In line with the new budget, I recommend Capitech Ltd.
opts.why: Not appropriate: Myro Ltd need 24/7 access to a helpdesk.

opts.t: In line with the new budget, I recommend Alliance On-line.
opts.why: Second most effective: closest of the options that stays within £215 a month, with 69% performance only just short of the “preferable” 70%.

opts.t: In line with the new budget, I recommend DigiCorp.
opts.why: Most effective: Myro has more than 10 employees (13), so it qualifies for the 15% discount. With the discount, DigiCorp meets every requirement, whether preferable or non-negotiable.

opts.t: No response required.
opts.why: Most effective: the message was sent to ALL, not to the candidate personally, and needs nothing back. It shows effective prioritising within the time limit.

opts.t: Thank you for your message. Just letting you know that Odette Lawson’s name should be removed from the Entrepreneur Fast-Track team, as she is no longer an employee but remains listed on the Organogram.
opts.why: Least effective: the e-mail already says this will be fixed, and telling the HR director this could come across as patronising.

opts.t: This has been noted, thank you for the information.
opts.why: Second most effective: it acknowledges the message politely and courteously.

opts.t: Thank you for your message, where can I access the new Organogram?
opts.why: Not appropriate: Glen already says it is in the documents section, so this suggests the candidate did not read the message properly.

opts.t: Perhaps the EFT department could implement a Team-Building exercise, such as “All Ears”.
opts.why: Not appropriate: Alan wants to focus on communication and resilience, which this exercise does not target (Document 6).

opts.t: Perhaps the EFT department could implement a Team-Building exercise, such as “Green Shoots”.
opts.why: Most effective: it targets what Alan asked for and has the highest success rate. The employee profiles also show Alan is a fan of group cohesion exercises.

opts.t: Perhaps the EFT department could implement a Team-Building exercise, such as “Marble Run”.
opts.why: Second most effective: it targets communication and resilience but has a lower success rate than Green Shoots.

opts.t: Perhaps in time the team will get settled, these things often work themselves out.
opts.why: Least effective: it does not address the issues in the e-mail and fails to support the Director’s efforts, even though he is clearly keen on group cohesion exercises.

opts.t: I am afraid I do not feel comfortable discussing this with you, as you are not the department Director.
opts.why: Not appropriate: it is impolite. Anthony is not the Director, but he is still the candidate’s superior.

opts.t: Unfortunately I would be inclined to agree, as I have already had to correct one of his mistakes regarding Myro Limited’s monthly budget for a technical support system.
opts.why: Least effective: it judges a colleague unfairly and harms morale. It is also unclear whether Robert had already corrected the mistake, as the message was forwarded by someone else.

opts.t: I have not seen any conclusive evidence of this as yet, but I will contact you if I do.
opts.why: Second most effective: it answers Anthony’s concern without judging another employee prematurely.

opts.t: I have not seen any conclusive evidence of this, but if I do I will mention his performance during my meeting with Alan Walker next week.
opts.why: Most effective: it answers Anthony’s concern without premature judgement, and gives the candidate time to reflect and raise the issue with the most appropriate person if needed.

items.t: E-mail 10: Amanda Dunn – Cohesion exercises for the EFT team

opts.t: Having looked through the information, the best option would be a combination of “Green Shoots” and “Marble Run”.
opts.why: Not appropriate: Alan wants to improve Communication, Trust, Collaboration and Resilience, and these two exercises do not cover all four.

opts.t: Having looked through the information, the best option would be a combination of “All Ears” and “Marble Run”.
opts.why: Second most effective: it meets every requirement but has a lower success rate than the best pair.

opts.t: Having looked through the information, the best option would be a combination of “All Ears” and “Green Shoots”.
opts.why: Most effective: the time for All Ears reduces with fewer participants. With only six members of Entrepreneur Fast-Track, this pair meets every requirement and has the highest success rate.

opts.t: No response is required, as I already gave my suggestion in a previous message.
opts.why: Least effective: it does not address the request and fails to support the Director’s efforts.
